The charge is distributed uniformly throughout the sphere so we can apply Gauss’s law to find the electric field. Let’s choose a spherical Gaussian surface of radius r, concentric with the sphere, as shown in figure a.

The line of charge is infinitely long. Therefore, the field is the same at all points equidistant from the line, regardless of the vertical position of the point in figure 20.19 a.
